program.section_heading: Administration of Justice/Corrections - Associate of Science Degree - MAS932/MAS932B/MAS932C
outcomes: Identify the basic safety components of working in a correctional facility, including, but not limited to inmate safety, personal safety and facility safety.
Demonstrate an understanding of the importance of classification of inmates.
Identify the key liability issues that impact the individual correctional officer and the facility as a whole.
Interpret codes, statutes, and policies as they relate to the care and custody of inmates in a correctional facility.
Apply principles and tactics to maintain control and security while working with groups of inmates in a correctional facility.

notes: The 'Units: 18.00' printed under the 'Required Courses' heading appears to cover the whole program (ADJ-C1D 15 + one 3-unit elective) and matches 'Total : 18.00'; it was recorded as the program total rather than as the stated total of the ADJ-C1D block.
ADJ-22 (Legal Aspects of Corrections) is listed in the catalog but not in the closed list; recorded as a catalog addition.
Footnote markers (* and **) are printed without clear attachment to specific courses; footnotes refer to California Board of Corrections and Rehabilitation mandates.
General education is required per the degree statement but no specific GE pattern is named, so ge_pattern is null.
The heading line also lists program codes MAS932/C; the fuller heading MAS932/MAS932B/MAS932C was used as the section heading.
